q-164425.name: Question 1
q-164425.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}=1?$
q-164425.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\frac{{x}^{2}}{25}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{9}=1\}
$$

which can be written as

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\frac{{x}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}+\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{{3}^{2}}=1\}.
$$

This is an ellipse centered at $(0,3)$ with semi-axes of lengths $5$ and $3.$

q-164422.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the parabolic cylinder $(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3)?$
q-164422.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our parabolic cylinder is

$$
(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3),\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:(y-3)^{2}=2(x+3)\}.
$$

This is a rightward-opening parabola with a vertex at $(-3,3).$

Question 3
?

What is the domain in the xy-plane of the hyperbolic cylinder (x+5)2−y2=1?

a
A hyperbola centered at (−5,0)
b
A hyperbola centered at (5,0)
c
R2
d
{(x,y)∈R2:xy=1}
e
A hyperbola centered at (5,1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The full expression describing all points on our hyperbolic cylinder is (x+5)2−y2=1,z=k where k∈R can vary arbitrarily.

The domain of any cylinder in the xy-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is {(x,y)∈R2: (x+5)2−y2=1}.

This is a hyperbola centered at (−5,0).

q-164424.name: Question 4
q-164424.problem: What is the domain in the $xy$-plane of the elliptic cylinder $\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{36}=1?$
q-164424.worked_solution:
The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

$$
\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{36}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{4}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{36}=1\}
$$

which can be written as

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\frac{(x-4)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}+\frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{6}^{2}}=1\}.
$$

This is an ellipse centered at $(4,2)$ with semi-axes of lengths $2$ and $6.$

The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

$$
\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}=1,\,z=k
$$

where $k\in R$ can vary arbitrarily. 

The domain of any cylinder in the $xy$-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

$$
\{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}:\text{ }\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{16}+\frac{(y+2)^{2}}{8}=1\}

$$

q-35569.html:
Question 5
?

What is the domain in the xy-plane of the elliptic cylinder (x−1)216+(y+2)28=1?

a
The interior and boundary of an ellipse centered at (1,−2) with semi-axes of lengths 4 and 22.
b
An ellipse centered at (1,−2) with semi-axes of lengths 4 and 22.
c
The interior and boundary of an ellipse centered at (1,2) with semi-axes of lengths 4 and 2.
d
An ellipse centered at (−1,2) with semi-axes of lengths 2 and 22.
e
An ellipse centered at (1,−2) with semi-axes of lengths 2 and 4.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The full expression describing all points on our elliptic cylinder is

(x−1)216+(y+2)28=1,z=k where k∈R can vary arbitrarily.

The domain of any cylinder in the xy-plane is its base curve. Hence, in this case, the domain is

{(x,y)∈R2: (x−1)216+(y+2)28=1}

which can be written as

{(x,y)∈R2: (x−1)242+(y+2)2(22)2=1}.

This is an ellipse centered at (1,−2) with semi-axes of lengths 4 and 22.

q-164414.name: Question 6
q-164414.problem: The projection of the intersection between the parabolic cylinder $4(x-3)^{2}=12(z+1)$ and the plane $y=2$ onto the $xz$-plane is a parabola. What is the vertex of the parabola?
q-164414.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane $y=2,$ we substitute $y=2$ into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) $y$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-3)^{2} & =12(z+1) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =3(z+1) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =4\cdot \frac{3}{4}\cdot (z+1).\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a parabola in the $xz$-plane with the vertex at $(3,-1).$

Question 6

The projection of the intersection between the parabolic cylinder 4(x−3)2=12(z+1) and the plane y=2 onto the xz-plane is a parabola. What is the vertex of the parabola?

a
(2,−1)
b
(−3,1)
c
(3,2)
d
(3,−1)
e
(3,1)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane y=2, we substitute y=2 into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) y term, we get

4(x−3)2=12(z+1)(x−3)2=3(z+1)(x−3)2=4⋅34⋅(z+1).

This gives us the equation of a parabola in the xz-plane with the vertex at (3,−1).

q-164413.name: Question 7
q-164413.problem: The projection of the intersection between the elliptic cylinder $2(y-1)^{2}+4(z+3)^{2}=16$ and the plane $x=3$ onto the $yz$-plane is an ellipse. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the ellipse?
q-164413.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane $x=3,$ we substitute $x=3$ into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) $x$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(y-1)^{2}+4(z+3)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{8}+\frac{(z+3)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{(z+3)^{2}}{(2)^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with semi-axes of lengths $2\sqrt{2}$ and $2.$

Question 7

The projection of the intersection between the elliptic cylinder 2(y−1)2+4(z+3)2=16 and the plane x=3 onto the yz-plane is an ellipse. What are the lengths of the semi-axes of the ellipse?

a
22 and 2
b
2 and 8
c
22 and 16
d
1 and 2
e
8 and 16
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane x=3, we substitute x=3 into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) x term, we get

2(y−1)2+4(z+3)2=16(y−1)28+(z+3)24=1(y−1)2(22)2+(z+3)2(2)2=1.

This gives us the equation of an ellipse with semi-axes of lengths 22 and 2.

q-164412.problem: The projection of the intersection between the parabolic cylinder $3(x+2)^{2}=6(y+3)$ and the plane $z=4$ onto the $xy$-plane is a parabola. What is the vertex of the parabola?
q-164412.worked_solution:
To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane $z=4,$ we substitute $z=4$ into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) $z$ term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x+2)^{2} & =6(y+3) \\ (x+2)^{2} & =2(y+3) \\ (x+2)^{2} & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}\cdot (y+3).\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us the equation of a parabola in the $xy$-plane with the vertex at $(-2,-3).$

The projection of the intersection between the parabolic cylinder 3(x+2)2=6(y+3) and the plane z=4 onto the xy-plane is a parabola. What is the vertex of the parabola?

a
(−3,2)
b
(4,−3)
c
(2,3)
d
(−2,−3)
e
(−2,4)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the intersection of the cylinder and the plane z=4, we substitute z=4 into the equation of the cylinder. However, since the equation has no (explicit) z term, we get

3(x+2)2=6(y+3)(x+2)2=2(y+3)(x+2)2=4⋅12⋅(y+3).

This gives us the equation of a parabola in the xy-plane with the vertex at (−2,−3).
